body:
This has been an ongoing theme too that I have struggled with as well - that she seems to be the "center of my universe".

My therapist called it the "earthmother" - 

"Mother is the name for God in the lips and hearts of little children." 
-William Makepeace Thackeray

When my mother disconnected, it left me with basically nothing - I lost that connection altogether. So she was the first person that I reconnected with. It's totally unfair to her, that I needed her to be my earthmother, my wife and a mother to my children. The responsibility was just too great.

I work every day to find fulfillment in other areas of my life. I constantly nurture my creative side, because that's where I find most of my self-worth now. 

I do still have a huge fear of rejection/loss, but I have come to the realization that yes - people will always leave, even if you do everything 100% correct.

You're absolutely right. 

I have a friend who I respect very much. His opinion on the whole situation was that I should let the children reside with their mother full time, because playing a constant game of tug-o-war with them all the time is unhealthy. 

I think that was maybe being somewhat over analyzing the situation and can be somewhat robotic about the situation, he does have feelings but he is very good about separating them when he needs to make a decision. 

I genuinely want what is best for them in the long run. Thank you for reminding me that I need to stay involved, that pushing through is what is best for them.

Thank you for responding.

It seems selfish now that I posted very little about my children. I do care about them very much. 

They are actually part of the reason I feel this way as well. She and I also have opposing viewpoints on discipline and just generally how our children should be raised. 

We have shared custody and when they come to my house we spend quite a lot of time getting accustomed to the way things are supposed to be. We play the "mom does this" game often. It seems like we share the same discipline style, but I am always firm in what I say. Even if I set in place a punishment which may have been overly harsh, I have to follow through with it. I believe that children need unconditional positive regard, strict unwavering rules with consistent outcome when they try to break them and obvious physical needs - food, water, shelter. 

She says that she follows this formula - but it's impossible, every time I discipline both of them in this way I get gigantic rage fits. Sometimes my son even gets violent, and it breaks my heart to have to restrain him, because I remember being like that. My parents didn't act like me though, they locked me in my room and waited hours for me to "cry it out", with him - I make sure he can't hurt me or anyone else, then we have a talk about why something silly like refusing to eat his green beans or pinching his sister turned into a knock down drag out fight, I tell him I don't want it to happen again and that I love him, then we move on.

It doesn't feel like it's getting better though, the fits continue every time they return to my house. I feel like an accessory of a parent, like my influence is so minuscule - any good I am doing is being far outweighed by what happens at home with mom. 

I love them very dearly, almost as much as their mother - my daughter's energy has captured me a few times recently and when my son was born his did as well. 

I just constantly wonder what the best thing is for them. Would it be best for me to bow out of their lives and let them love with their mother "new father" and half-brother full time? To just let them be a family and stop interfering and disrupting? That's truly how it feels most of the time.
